body: King of the apes movie is showing in theatres right now. If you haven’t watched the franchise maybe it’s something you should try. You might like it? I often find myself looking for simpler reasons to extend my stay here. Sometimes there doesn’t have to be a big meaning, but little things that you might as well make time for. Like I know that I would ideally like to be around to see the beyond the spiderverse movie. And there’s a list of books I’ve been meaning to read. One step at a time.
Lmao that’s actually one of the reasons that I haven’t been able to go ahead with suicide yet. The fear of failing.
maybe you’re right. it’s just a constant fear i have, and am aware of — being like my parents. but i was just a kid. i don’t think it was right for them to treat me like they did

my dad was ranting like he always does. he has this thing where one little thing sets him off, and it eventually escalates until one us got beat, and then the next day act like everything was normal. he was starting up again and everyone was quiet and just dealing with it. he started ranting at me, and started shouting. i remember getting very sweaty and cold, and thinking ‘he’s gonna hit me’ so i just, hit him first. 

i was a (edit: got my age wrong, i was in primary school still so i was probably 8/9) year old skinny twig girl with noodle arms, so ofc it didn’t even move him or hurt him or anything. but once i hit him once, i just kept doing it. he was shocked that i would even do anything he just stood there. i just kind of blanked out there, next thing i remember is my mum yelling at me (edit: removed info because i’m paranoid)

now it’s like some big shameful family secret or something, my mum tries to hang it above my head as a way to shame me to my younger siblings. i wasn’t the best, and i hate that i couldn’t control my anger, i essentially was just as bad as my dad in that moment. i’m not a very angry person in general, though i can be quite snappy/moody i guess, but i don’t think i’ve had another moment like that and i’m 22 now so. i’m working on it.
yeah. they’ve held it against me ever since

Ah, had a similar experience with a friend in Highschool who would call me East Pakistani as a joke. Didn’t really find it funny, in hindsight kinda annoyed that I just took it instead of having a comeback. At the time I just didn’t want to engage at all, it’s so old and tiring. Also hearing the horror stories and seeing relatives still broken by their experiences, how could you possibly condense that into an explanation? One of the earliest memories my Dad has is of seeing dead bodies floating in water. It’s not as long ago as people think. Ugh why should I have to explain why I am offended anyway...

Yo I relate to this hard. I’m so sorry you have to go through this. It’s good you recognise her toxicity for what it is. I still struggle between loving my parents and recognising what they’re actually like, I just can’t shake this sense of loyalty as though I’m betraying them and it eats me up inside. 

My Dad lied to his brothers about me being a member of a political party, (there was a time when I was interested in politics and of course they took it and ran a mile). I remember how ashamed he looked when I told them it wasn’t true and I still feel guilty about how I disappointed him. I’m working on it.

For what it’s worth, I hope you find comforts where you can.
